message.reasoning:
I am ready to play Monopoly and make a decision.

I am analyzing the board. I have $847 and three unmortgaged properties on the pink group. I am checking opponent holdings to assess trade opportunities.

p1 holds St. James and Tennessee on the orange group, plus Kentucky and Illinois on red. He also owns Water Works, Marvin Gardens, and Short Line. I need to acquire Virginia to complete the pink monopoly.

p2 has a dangerous dark blue monopoly with three houses on Park Place and Boardwalk. p4 holds a light blue monopoly and cash of $869. I am weighing trade, mortgage, or end turn.

The Marvin Gardens trade with p1 is dead. I rejected their $450 offer and they did not counter again. Landing on Park Place or Boardwalk would bankrupt me at $847, so I need to mortgage or move away from that threat.

Mortgaging my pink properties would only raise cash to $1017, still below the $1100 and $1400 rent from p2's dark blue monopoly. p2 can easily add a fourth house there. p4 can also build on his light blue group, and I am currently on Vermont which he can target.

I am weighing the pink group as my main target. Virginia is unowned and costs $160, which I can afford with my current cash. Building there would be expensive, but it is a stronger prize than the brown group. The brown group would need Mediterranean Avenue to complete, which is too weak to justify the investment.

I am ruling out trades with p4 and p2. p4 needs Marvin Gardens to complete his yellow monopoly, so I should not give it away or help him build. p2 already holds dark blue and would use any cash I offered to add another house.

I am reconsidering the Marvin Gardens trade with p1. At $450, I would have only about $567 left after mortgaging my pink properties. That is risky against p4's light blue builds. I also realize Marvin does not complete a set for me, so blocking p4's yellow monopoly may not be worth that price.

A fully built yellow monopoly would be extremely lethal. If p1 sells Marvin to p4, p4 would hold two monopolies plus railroads and become the favorite to win. I am now exploring whether a trade with p1 could help both of us against p2 and p4 instead of paying $450 for a single property.

I am now looking at p1's own needs. He needs New York for his orange monopoly and Indiana from p2 for red. I am also considering whether to propose a trade with p4 that does not help him build.

I have ruled out all trade options. p4 already holds a complete light blue monopoly and nothing I need. p1 will not sell Marvin cheaply. I will not give p2 cash. I will not mortgage my pink properties. The only remaining choice is to end the turn.

I am reconsidering one last trade with p1. I would offer $300 for Marvin Gardens and warn that if p4 buys it, p4 could build yellow and kill p1 too. p1 is cash-poor at $137 and has just paid rent on Pennsylvania Avenue.

I checked p1's mortgageable assets. He can raise cash without my help, so he does not need my money. I am now weighing a $350 to $400 offer for Marvin. That would leave me with about $617 after mortgaging my pink properties, but it would block p4's yellow monopoly permanently and still prevent me from buying Virginia.

I realized that buying Marvin would make me more vulnerable to p4. With $447 left, I cannot survive a fully improved light blue group, and p4 already holds one that he may be saving to build. Paying $350–$400 for the property would drain my cash and give him the incentive to construct it.

I cannot outbid p4 for Marvin at $450 without bankrupting my defense. If I buy it for $300 and p1 accepts, I will hold the deed and refuse to sell it to p4.

I am now calculating the maximum price I should pay for Marvin as a pure block against p4's yellow monopoly. I also realize that if I offer $300 and p1 rejects it, I will still get another decision because the engine updates the state and asks again.

Fully improved yellow would be more lethal than light blue because of higher rent, but it costs $150 per house versus $50 for light blue. p4 has $869 and could build light blue to three houses and still have $419 left, or build hotels and have $119 left. He might also buy Marvin for $400 and build both monopolies partially. If I do not acquire Marvin first, p4 could trade with p1 to get it and then build yellow.

I am checking the exact rent values for the yellow group. A fully improved yellow monopoly would cost p4 $1350, which exceeds his $869 cash. I am now calculating whether one house on each property is enough to threaten me.

I have confirmed the exact rent values for each property. p2's dark blue monopoly already charges $1100 on Park Place and $1400 on Boardwalk, which is lethal to almost anyone. p1 has only $137 in cash, so he cannot survive any improved property. p4 has $869, which is still too little to cover those dark blue rents even with mortgages.

I calculated p4's total liquid assets at roughly $1649. He can survive one hit from p2's dark blue monopoly by mortgaging almost all of his properties, though this would un-monopolize his light blue set.

Mortgaging the light blue set would temporarily kill p4's monopoly. I cannot survive dark blue, so the game is a race to avoid landing on it. p4 building light blue is the more immediate threat after dark blue. Three houses on Connecticut would cost $450, which I can afford with $847. Hotels would raise that to $600.

I will end the turn. I rejected a $250 offer for Marvin and will not raise the price further. I cannot trade for Virginia or Mediterranean Avenue, and p4 does not hold it. I will send a brief public message without revealing strategy.

I considered selling Baltic Avenue for cash, but it is nearly worthless without Mediterranean and I might land on it later. I also rejected a trade with p2 because any cash I gave him would only let him buy another house.

I will not offer p1 any protection or partnership against p4, since the tools only allow property, cash, or jail card trades. I will end the turn and keep my public message brief and strategic, perhaps hinting that I am no longer interested in Marvin so p4 might try to acquire it from p1 instead.
